short: Kaldi DNN-HMM cuts SSC WER from 17.4% to 6.45% (M06, M12: standard), but with the same bigram its own GMM gives 12.71%, so the DNN halves WER; one speaker, single runs.
position: The paper [@ji2018updating] changes the recognizer (M06), a Kaldi DNN-HMM plus deep-autoencoder (DAE) features, and resets the Silent Speech Challenge (SSC) reference number (M12). Both are standard: the same group had already run a DNN-HMM on the SSC (38% WER, §1.2), and a multimodal DAE on tongue and lip images predates it [@jaumardhakoun2016articulatory]. The drop from 17.4% to 6.45% WER holds, but with the same WSJ bigram the paper's own LDA+MLLT triphone GMM reaches 12.71% (Table 3), so against its best GMM the DNN halves the WER rather than cutting it by "almost a factor of 3" (inference). The number is tied to one speaker, 1023 test words, single runs and a closed 5,000-word bigram; an end-to-end model with a 65,000-word language model reached 20.5% on the same test [@kimura2020end]. The DAE's advantage at 5 dimensions rests on DCT systems that fail outright (98.24% to 100% WER), a collapse the paper leaves unexplained, so it does not show the DAE keeps information DCT loses.
